newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel tears down nine illegally built Arab homes.
newsitem.headline: Israel tears down nine illegally built Arab homes.

text.p: Israel on Wednesday demolished nine Arab homes in East Jerusalem and in the West Bank it said had been built illegally, Israeli spokesmen said.
The wave of demolitions coincided with summit talks between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein in the Jordanian Red Sea resort of Aqaba.

An Israeli Jerusalem municipality spokeswoman said five homes were destroyed in East Jerusalem and a spokesman for Israel's West Bank occupation authorities said four homes were wrecked in the Bethlehem area.
"This morning five structures were demolished. All five of them were foundations, they were all built without permits," the Jerusalem spokeswoman said.
"They were built on a valley that was not planned for housing units and will never be planned for housing," she said.
She said the homes near the Arab village of Anata were built on public land and were only partially constructed. Witnesses said a few Arabs threw stones at Israeli soldiers and workers near the site.
The spokeswoman said no Israeli construction was planned for the area.
Palestinians say they are forced to build illegally because the municipality will not give them permits. They accuse Israel of trying to drive them out of Jerusalem.

The municipality says Arabs have built more than 2,600 buildings without permits in the past two years. Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert has called illegal Arab building a "cancer" that threatens Israel's sovereignty in the holy city.

"Today we demolished four houses that were illegally built in the Bethlehem district...All demolitions had passed all procedures according to the law," said Peter Lerner, spokesman of the Israeli authorities in the West Bank and Gaza.

The Jerusalem municipality says it has approved 75 percent of 504 applications to build in Arab neighbourhoods in the past two years. It says it has approved 90 percent of 2,893 applications to build in Jewish neighbourhoods.

This year, the municipality has issued 17 orders to destroy homes in East Jerusalem and has carried out nine of them. The city said it had torn down parts of seven Jewish homes that were built without permits.
Israel captured East Jerusalem from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East war and later annexed it in a move that failed to win international recognition.

Palestinians want East Jerusalem for the capital of a future state. They say Israeli demolitions and construction of Jewish homes in East Jerusalem are aimed at preempting future "final status" peace talks on the city's fate slated to end in 1999.
Israel says it will never cede any part of Jerusalem and has the right to do as it pleases in the city it claims as its "eternal capital".
